grammarDeepDive.title: Countable vs uncountable — quando contar, quando não
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Em inglês, palavras como sugar, water, rice são incontáveis: não têm plural e não usam a/an. Já bag, box, truck são contáveis: viram plural com -s.

Com contáveis use many / a few. Com incontáveis use much / a little. Some vai em afirmativas; any em negativas e perguntas.

Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar, Units 75–76.
Cambridge Dictionary — countable and uncountable nouns.

lessons.title: Late or On Time? — Atrasado ou no Horário?
lessons.objective: Descrever entregas e motoristas usando adjetivos comuns.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Adjectives tell you everything you need to know in half a sentence: a late delivery, a heavy truck, a safe driver. Today we put them in the right order and use them like a Londoner.

vocab.example: The driver is fast, but always safe — never reckless.
The route is long today — 320 kilometres to the client.
The truck is heavy — just under 22 tonnes fully loaded.
The gate is narrow — reverse slowly.
The morning is quiet; the afternoon is usually busy.

lessons.situation: Harry fala com Emily sobre os motoristas que chegaram atrasados ou no horário.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Adjetivos vêm antes do substantivo ou depois do verbo to be.
• a fast truck
• the truck is fast

💛 Em inglês, o adjetivo é sempre invariável (não tem plural).

takeaways: Adjectives describe nouns.
They come before the noun: a heavy truck.
They don't change form: good man, good woman.
"Very" adds strength, sparingly.
"A bit" softens: a bit late.
"Quite" is also a softener.
Pair adjectives with and: big and heavy.
Avoid too many adjectives in one sentence.
Clear adjectives = faster decisions.
Know the basics: late, early, safe, fast, slow.

lessonFlow.instructions:
OBJETIVO DE HOJE (diga em português, devagar): Descrever entregas e motoristas usando adjetivos comuns.

Escreva no quadro o título da aula: "Late or On Time?".

Aquecimento sem pressão — pergunte em inglês, com sorriso, aceitando respostas de uma palavra:
  • "Hello! How are you today?"
  • "Are you ready to start?"
  • "Today: logistics. Easy and slow, ok?"

💛 Regra de ouro do nível Confidence: o aluno é iniciante. Fale devagar, repita, e elogie cada tentativa. Errar faz parte.

Apresente as 5 palavras-chave. Para cada palavra: você diz, o aluno repete 2x, depois você dá a tradução.

  • slow = lento
  • safe = seguro
  • busy = ocupado / movimentado
  • empty = vazio

  • The route is long today — 320 kilometres to the client.
  • The truck is heavy — just under 22 tonnes fully loaded.

Cheque o entendimento apontando/perguntando: "What is this? (truck / warehouse...)". Aceite a palavra solta — o importante é reconhecer.

lessons.title: Phone Calls from Drivers — Ligações dos Motoristas
lessons.objective: Atender ligações dos motoristas e fazer pedidos polidos com can e could.
lessons.intro:
💛 Dica: educação abre todas as portas (e cancelas).

Drivers call the office all day long — for help, for information, for permission. Can and could are the polite hinges of every one of those calls. Today we make sure they swing smoothly.

vocab.example: The driver's call came in just before noon — a flat tyre near the port.
Can you help me find the spare key? I can't find it anywhere.
Could you repeat the address, please? The line is bad.
The answer is always the same: safety first, schedule second.
Please hold — I'll check with the dispatcher and call you straight back.

Can e could são verbos modais. Não levam -s na 3ª pessoa e vêm seguidos de verbo no infinitivo sem to.

lessons.title: Simple Invoices — Notas Simples

lessons.intro:

💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Every shift needs a short, honest report at the end. Today we use was / were, the past of to be, to describe how things went. Clear past-tense reports are the foundation of every good improvement.

The weather was perfect for the long route.

lessons.objective: Falar sobre clima e trânsito usando a estrutura It is + adjetivo.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Weather and traffic shape every delivery. A short phrase — "it's raining," "the traffic is heavy" — can save hours. Today we practise the structure It is + weather / traffic so you can brief any driver in seconds.

The traffic is heavy this morning because of the football.
It's foggy near the river — slow down before the bridge.
The road is clear between junctions 8 and 12.
It's very windy today — watch the trailer on the flyover.

lessonFlow.instructions:
OBJETIVO DE HOJE (diga em português, devagar): Comparar rotas, caminhões e motoristas usando comparativos simples.

Escreva no quadro o título da aula: "Fast, Slow, Safe".

Aquecimento sem pressão — pergunte em inglês, com sorriso, aceitando respostas de uma palavra:

Apresente as 5 palavras-chave. Para cada palavra: você diz, o aluno repete 2x, depois você dá a tradução.

  • cheaper = mais barato
  • better = melhor

Leia estes exemplos em voz alta (o aluno repete):
  • The new truck is faster than the old one by about 15%.
  • The coastal route is longer but safer than the mountain road.
  • A full trailer is slower than a half-loaded one on hills.

Cheque o entendimento apontando/perguntando: "What is this? (truck / warehouse...)". Aceite a palavra solta — o importante é reconhecer.

Foco gramatical: Comparativos — fast, faster, safer.

Comparativos.
• Adjetivos curtos + -er: fast → faster, slow → slower.
• Adjetivos longos: more + adj: more expensive.
• Irregulares: good → better, bad → worse.
Use than: This route is faster than that one.

grammarDeepDive.title: Comparatives — comparar em inglês
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Para comparar, usamos o comparativo:

• Adjetivos curtos: adicione -er e use than: fast → faster than.
• Adjetivos longos (3+ sílabas): use more + adj + than: more expensive than.
• Irregulares: good → better, bad → worse, far → farther/further.

💛 Adjetivos terminados em consoante + y trocam y por i: busy → busier.

lessons.title: Problems with the Truck — Problemas com o Caminhão
lessons.objective: Relatar problemas e soluções no passado usando o Simple Past.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Every truck has a bad day now and then. Today we use the Simple Past of regular verbs to tell those stories clearly: what happened, when, and what we did about it.

vocab.example: The truck arrived two hours late because of a broken alternator.
The driver called us as soon as the warning light appeared.
The mechanic checked the engine and replaced the part within an hour.
We rescheduled the delivery for the same afternoon, not the next day.
The client thanked us for the quick and honest update.

lessons.grammarDetail:
Simple Past — verbos regulares terminam em -ed.

• fix → fixed

takeaways: Regular verbs add -ed: call → called.
Verbs ending in -e add only -d: arrive → arrived.
-y becomes -ied: try → tried.
Double final consonant sometimes: stop → stopped.
Pronunciation of -ed varies: /t/, /d/, /ɪd/.
Use with past time markers.
Honest past reports build trust.
Include what you did, not just what broke.
A good report explains what changed for next time.
Every problem is a lesson if you write it down.

grammarDeepDive.title: Simple Past — verbos regulares com -ed
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Para formar o passado simples de verbos regulares, acrescente -ed ao verbo: work → worked, call → called.

Regras de ortografia:
• Verbos com consoante + y: troque y por i + ed: try → tried.
• Verbos CVC curtos (stop): dobre a consoante + ed: stop → stopped.

💛 A pronúncia de -ed varia: /t/ (stopped), /d/ (called), /ɪd/ (waited).
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use, Units 11–12.
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar, Unit 15.
Cambridge Grammar — Simple past.

lessons.objective: Agradecer, elogiar e ser educado em inglês no ambiente de trabalho.
lessons.intro:
💛 Dica: um "thank you" sincero vale mais que mil e-mails.

Drivers do the hardest part of logistics — long hours, long roads, difficult weather. Today we practise the polite expressions that turn a boss into a colleague and a colleague into a friend.

Your calm reaction to the breakdown made all the difference.

grammarDeepDive.title: Polite expressions — educação no trabalho
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Em inglês, please, thank you e sorry são muito usadas — até mais que em português!

• Please — por favor (em pedidos).
• Thank you / Thanks — obrigado.
• Sorry — desculpa (por um erro).
• Excuse me — com licença (para interromper).
• You're welcome / No problem — de nada.

💛 Dica: um "thank you" sincero vale mais que mil palavras técnicas.
references: Cambridge Dictionary — polite expressions.
Swan, M. — Practical English Usage, entry 'politeness'.
Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary — please/thank you.

lessons.title: A Day in My Delivery Life — Um Dia na Minha Vida de Entregas
lessons.objective: Contar um dia típico de trabalho combinando todos os tópicos do nível Confidence.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: cada entrega é um capítulo. Cada dia, um livro novo.

This final lesson of the Logistics track is a full day in your delivery life — from 5 am at the gate to the last signed note in the evening. We'll review to be, Present Simple, there is/are, prepositions, modals and past tense — all in one natural story.

vocab.example: Every day in delivery starts with a list and ends with a signed note.
There are always surprises — the job is to handle them calmly.
I have learned more in this year than in all my previous jobs.
We celebrate on-time deliveries and we learn from the late ones.
The small gestures — a thank-you, a clear invoice — build the bigger trust.

takeaways: A good day starts with a clear plan.
Every truck, every pallet, every invoice has a place.

Politeness keeps the team strong under pressure.
Write down what goes wrong — and what fixed it.

lessonFlow.instructions:
OBJETIVO DE HOJE (diga em português, devagar): Contar um dia típico de trabalho combinando todos os tópicos do nível Confidence.

Escreva no quadro o título da aula: "A Day in My Delivery Life".

Aquecimento sem pressão — pergunte em inglês, com sorriso, aceitando respostas de uma palavra:
  • "Hello! How are you today?"
  • "Are you ready to start?"
  • "Today: logistics. Easy and slow, ok?"

💛 Regra de ouro do nível Confidence: o aluno é iniciante. Fale devagar, repita, e elogie cada tentativa. Errar faz parte.

Apresente as 5 palavras-chave. Para cada palavra: você diz, o aluno repete 2x, depois você dá a tradução.

  • routine = rotina
  • goal = meta
  • team = time
  • proud = orgulhoso
  • learn = aprender

Leia estes exemplos em voz alta (o aluno repete):
  • Every day in delivery starts with a list and ends with a signed note.
  • There are always surprises — the job is to handle them calmly.
  • I have learned more in this year than in all my previous jobs.

Cheque o entendimento apontando/perguntando: "What is this? (truck / warehouse...)". Aceite a palavra solta — o importante é reconhecer.

Foco gramatical: Revisão geral — Confidence / Logistics.

Revisão. Combine to be, Present Simple, preposições, dias e expressões polidas para contar seu dia. Ex.: On Monday, I start at 7 AM. I check the trucks, then I call the drivers. The traffic is heavy but we arrive on time.

Frases-modelo (escreva no quadro e leia junto):
  • A good day starts with a clear plan.
  • Every truck, every pallet, every invoice has a place.
  • Short radio messages save long problems.

Drill rápido (5 min): você diz em português, o aluno tenta em inglês. Corrija com carinho e repita a forma certa em voz alta.

Façam JUNTOS os exercícios da lição (role a tela até a seção de exercícios). Deixe o aluno tentar primeiro, depois confira. Gabarito abaixo para você não precisar procurar:

  1. Leia em voz alta
  2. Complete o texto
     Gabarito: a) am; b) at; c) from; to; d) have; e) is; f) are; g) was; h) Thank you; i) am; j) is
  3. Vocabulário
     Gabarito: a) routine; b) goal; c) team; d) proud; e) learn; f) routine; g) team; h) learn; i) proud; j) goal

Dica: se travar, dê a primeira letra ou leia a frase inteira pausando no espaço em branco para o aluno completar.

Hora de FALAR. Faça as perguntas abaixo em voz alta. Se o aluno travar, dê a resposta-modelo e peça para ele repetir e depois adaptar:

  • Pergunte: "What is today's topic?"
     Resposta-modelo: Today's topic is A Day in My Delivery Life — Um Dia na Minha Vida de Entregas.
  • Pergunte: "Who is the teacher?"
     Resposta-modelo: The teacher is Emily.
  • Pergunte: "Where does this happen?"
     Resposta-modelo: At the Czarnikow logistics team.
  • Pergunte: "How do you feel about this topic?"
     Resposta-modelo: I feel more confident about it now.
  • Pergunte: "Can you use it at work?"
     Resposta-modelo: Yes, I can use it every day at work.

Depois, façam o ROLE-PLAY da lição ("Praticando A Day in My Delivery Life — Um Dia na Minha Vida de Entregas"): você faz um papel, o aluno faz o outro, depois troquem. Use o diálogo-modelo que aparece no app como apoio.

Fechamento positivo. Peça ao aluno para dizer UMA frase com o que aprendeu hoje (ex.: "A good day starts with a clear plan.").

Feche com a afirmação de confiança: "Today I can talk about a day in my delivery life."

Mensagem final para o aluno: 💛 Parabéns! Você concluiu 20 lições de Logística Confidence. Você fala inglês!

Lição de casa (2 min): reler as 5 palavras de hoje em voz alta amanhã de manhã.

commonChallenges: Misturar tempos verbais — manter o foco no Presente ou Passado.
Esquecer do pronome antes do verbo.
Não usar expressões polidas — pratique thank you e please.

grammarDeepDive.title: Confidence review — juntando tudo
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Parabéns! Nesta lição revisamos todas as estruturas do nível Confidence aplicadas à logística:
• to be (am, is, are, was, were)
• Pronomes (I, you, he, she, it, we, they)
• there is / there are
• Present Simple
• Preposições (in, on, at, from, to)
• Contáveis/incontáveis (many, much, some, any)
• Imperativos (turn, go, take)
• Horários (at + time)
• Adjetivos e comparativos
• Modais (can, could)
• have / has
• Simple Past regular
• Wh- questions
• Expressões polidas

💛 Continue praticando 10 minutos por dia. Você já é um profissional bilíngue!
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge) — review units.
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar — review chapters.
Czarnikow English Programme — Confidence / Logistics syllabus.

lessons.title: Dias e Horários no Trabalho — Days at Work
lessons.objective: Aprender os dias da semana e usar on/at para falar da agenda no trabalho.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Today we learn the days of the week in English. At Czarnikow we use them every day — in meetings, emails and schedules. The week starts on Monday and ends on Sunday.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

vocab.example: The HR meeting is on Monday.
I work from home on Tuesday.
This week is very busy.
Have a nice weekend!
My schedule is full today.

lessons.situation: Sophie shows a new hire the HR weekly schedule and explains which days the team is in the office.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Dias da semana em inglês são escritos com letra maiúscula: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

Use on antes do dia: on Monday, on Friday. Use at com horas: at 9am, at noon.

💛 Sempre que falar de um dia, pense automaticamente "on". É um costume rápido de criar!

grammarDeepDive.title: Prepositions of time — on the day, at the hour
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Em inglês usamos on para dias específicos (on Monday, on my birthday) e at para horários (at 9am, at noon, at midnight).

Para partes do dia: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening, mas at night.

💛 Não traduza — memorize o bloco: on Monday at 9am.

lessons.title: Meu Papel na Empresa — My Role
lessons.grammar: Pronomes possessivos — my, your, his, her, our, their
lessons.objective: Usar pronomes possessivos para falar sobre o seu papel e o papel dos colegas na Czarnikow.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

In English, we use possessive pronouns to show who something belongs to: my job, your team, his office, her role. At Czarnikow, this helps us talk about roles clearly and kindly.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

vocab.example: My role is to support new hires.
Her manager is very kind.
My colleague is from Brazil.
Our department is HR.
His task is to send the report.

lessons.situation: Sophie introduces each person in the HR team and explains their role using possessive pronouns.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Pronomes possessivos: my (meu), your (seu), his (dele), her (dela), its (dele/dela coisa), our (nosso), their (deles).

Eles vêm antes do substantivo: my job, your team, his office, her role, our department, their task.

💛 Lembre: his para homem, her para mulher. Em português é igual (dele/dela), mas muda em inglês conforme a pessoa.

grammarDeepDive.title: Possessive adjectives — my, your, his, her, our, their
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Em inglês, os possessive adjectives não mudam com o substantivo — eles seguem a pessoa:
• I → my
• you → your
• he → his
• she → her
• it → its
• we → our
• they → their

Em português dizemos "o livro dela"; em inglês, her book — mais curto e direto.

💛 Cuidado: your (seu) ≠ you're (you are).
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online reference.

lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Greetings are the first moment of every conversation. At Czarnikow, a warm "Hello" and "Nice to meet you" open doors. Today you will learn 5 polite expressions that work every day.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

Goodbye, see you tomorrow.

Thanks for your help.

lessons.situation: Sophie meets new colleagues at reception and exchanges first greetings.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Apresentações simples:

• Nice to meet you — Prazer em conhecer você
• Nice to meet you too — Prazer em conhecer você também

• I am fine, thanks — Estou bem, obrigado(a).

💛 Um sorriso e um "Hi, nice to meet you" já abrem qualquer porta. Pratique 3 vezes em voz alta.

grammarDeepDive.title: Greetings — the first words of every conversation
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Em inglês, saudações funcionam em blocos: Hi + nome, How are you?, I am fine, thanks.

Para apresentações: Nice to meet you (primeiro encontro). Depois, use Good to see you (já se conheciam).

💛 Um "thanks" e um "please" pequenos transformam qualquer conversa.

grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Cardinal numbers são usados para contar. De 13 a 19, há o sufixo -teen: thirteen, fourteen, fifteen. Com 20: twenty.

lessons.title: O Dia de Trabalho — The Working Day
lessons.objective: Descrever a rotina diária de trabalho usando o Present Simple.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Every day at Czarnikow looks similar: we arrive, we check emails, we have meetings, we go home. To describe routines, English uses the Present Simple — the most common tense of all.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

vocab.example: I arrive at 9am.
I check my emails.
We start at 9.
I finish at 6pm.
I leave the office at 6.

lessons.situation: Sophie describes her typical day at Czarnikow from arrival to leaving.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Present Simple (rotina): I/you/we/they + verbo; he/she/it + verbo + s.
• I arrive at 9. / She arrives at 9.
• We check emails. / He checks emails.
• They finish at 6. / It finishes at 6.

💛 Para ele/ela/isso — sempre acrescente um -s ao verbo. Pratique: she arrives, he works, it starts.

grammarDeepDive.title: Present Simple — daily routines
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
O Present Simple é usado para rotinas, fatos e coisas que acontecem sempre.

• I / you / we / they + verbo: I arrive, we start
• he / she / it + verbo + s: she arrives, he starts, it finishes

Para verbos terminados em -ch, -sh, -x, -o: acrescente -es: she watches, he finishes, it goes.

💛 Um truque: pense "he/she/it = needs the S".

lessons.title: Perguntas Simples — Do / Does
lessons.grammar: Perguntas no Present Simple — Do you? Does he/she?
lessons.objective: Formular perguntas simples no Present Simple com Do / Does.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

To ask questions in the Present Simple, English uses Do and Does. Do for I/you/we/they; Does for he/she/it. These two words unlock hundreds of useful questions at work.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

vocab.example: I have a question.
The answer is yes.
Do you know Tom?
Does she work here?
Do you speak English?

lessons.situation: Sophie asks simple getting-to-know-you questions in the HR onboarding interview.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Perguntas no Present Simple:
• Do + I/you/we/they + verbo? → Do you work here?
• Does + he/she/it + verbo? → Does she work here?

Respostas curtas: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. / Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.

💛 Com Does, o verbo perde o -s! "Does she works" ❌ → "Does she work?" ✅

grammarDeepDive.title: Questions in the Present Simple — Do / Does
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Para fazer perguntas no Present Simple, adicionamos Do (I/you/we/they) ou Does (he/she/it) no início.

O verbo principal fica no infinitivo sem to: Do you work?, Does she work? (não "works"!).

Respostas curtas: Yes, I do / No, I don't; Yes, she does / No, she doesn't.

💛 Lembre: Does já "gasta" o s do verbo.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online reference.

lessons.title: Eu Gosto do Meu Trabalho — I like my job
lessons.objective: Falar sobre o que gosta e não gosta no trabalho usando like + -ing.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

At work, it is important to know what you like and what you don't. In English, we often say "I like + verb-ing": I like working, I like helping, I like learning. Simple and powerful.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

vocab.example: I like my job.
I enjoy helping people.
I prefer morning meetings.
I like learning new things.
I enjoy helping the team.

lessons.situation: Sophie asks new hires what they like about their role and what motivates them.
lessons.grammarDetail:
like + verbo-ing:
• I like working with people.
• She enjoys teaching.
• We prefer working from home on Fridays.

Também vale com enjoy e prefer. Não dizemos "I like to working" — é I like working.

💛 Regra de bolso: like + verbo terminando em -ing. Pratique: I like reading, I like talking, I like learning.

grammarDeepDive.title: Like / enjoy / prefer + -ing
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Em inglês, os verbos like, enjoy, prefer, love, hate costumam vir seguidos de verbo + -ing:

• I like working in a team.
• She enjoys teaching.
• We prefer starting early.

Também é possível I like to work, mas a forma mais comum é I like working.

💛 Na dúvida: like + -ing nunca erra.

lessons.title: Colegas e Departamentos — Plurals
lessons.objective: Formar plurais regulares para falar de pessoas e departamentos na Czarnikow.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

At Czarnikow there are many people and many departments. To talk about more than one, English uses plurals: colleague → colleagues, office → offices, box → boxes.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

vocab.example: My colleagues are kind.
We have offices in 13 countries.
The company has many departments.
The managers meet on Monday.
The reports are ready.

lessons.situation: Sophie lists the departments and counts people and offices around the world.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Plurais regulares:
• Acrescente -s: colleague → colleagues, office → offices
• Terminados em -s, -x, -ch, -sh: acrescente -es: box → boxes, watch → watches
• Terminados em consoante + y: y vira i + es: country → countries

💛 Mais de um? -s no fim. Simples assim!

grammarDeepDive.title: Regular plurals — +s, +es, y→ies
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
A maioria dos substantivos em inglês faz plural com -s: team → teams, day → days.

Terminados em -s, -x, -ch, -sh, -o geralmente ganham -es: box → boxes, watch → watches, tomato → tomatoes.

Quando termina em consoante + y, o y vira ies: country → countries, company → companies.

💛 Exceções vão aparecer (child → children), mas 95% dos plurais seguem essas regras.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online reference.

lessons.title: Que Horas São? — Telling Time
lessons.grammar: Telling the time — o'clock, half past, quarter past/to
lessons.objective: Dizer e entender horas em inglês no contexto de reuniões e agendas.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Time is gold in a global company. Today we practise "What time is it?" and answers like "It is nine o'clock", "It is half past ten", "It is quarter to five".

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

vocab.example: What time is it?
It is nine o'clock.
It is half past ten.
It is quarter past two.
Just one minute, please.

lessons.situation: Sophie tells the new hire the time of each meeting using different expressions.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Hours:
• 9:00 → It is nine o'clock.
• 9:15 → It is quarter past nine.
• 9:30 → It is half past nine.
• 9:45 → It is quarter to ten.
• 9:05 → It is five past nine.
• 9:50 → It is ten to ten.

💛 past = depois da hora; to = antes da próxima hora. Passou dos 30? Já é "to" para a hora seguinte.

grammarDeepDive.title: Telling the time — past and to
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Para dizer horas em inglês:
• o'clock para horas exatas: 3:00 → three o'clock.
• past para minutos após a hora (até 30): 3:20 → twenty past three.
• to para minutos antes da próxima hora (após 30): 3:40 → twenty to four.
• half past = meia hora depois; quarter past/to = 15 minutos.

💛 Em contextos digitais, também se aceita "It is nine thirty" ou "three forty".
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online reference.

lessons.title: Minha Semana — My Week
lessons.objective: Falar da rotina semanal usando advérbios de frequência (always, usually, sometimes, never).
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Some things we do every day; others, once a week. In English, we use frequency adverbs: always, usually, often, sometimes, never. They help us describe our week clearly.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

vocab.example: I always arrive at 9am.
I usually have lunch at 1.
I often meet the team.
I sometimes work from home.
I never skip the morning meeting.

lessons.situation: Sophie describes her weekly routine using frequency adverbs.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Advérbios de frequência vêm antes do verbo principal:
• I always arrive early.
• She usually checks emails.
• We sometimes work from home.
• I never skip lunch.

Com to be, o advérbio vem depois: She is always on time.

💛 Always, usually, often, sometimes, never — memorize nessa ordem de frequência (100% → 0%).

grammarDeepDive.title: Frequency adverbs — always, usually, often, sometimes, never
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Os advérbios de frequência dão informação sobre quantas vezes algo acontece.

Escala aproximada:
• always (100%)
• usually (90%)
• often (70%)
• sometimes (40%)
• rarely (15%)
• never (0%)

Posição: antes do verbo principal (I always arrive) e depois de to be (She is always on time).

💛 Use esses advérbios para falar de hábitos com precisão e naturalidade.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online reference.

lessons.objective: Dizer datas e meses em inglês para agendas, aniversários e eventos.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Months and dates are part of every HR calendar — birthdays, reviews, holidays. Today we learn the 12 months and the correct prepositions: in + month, on + date.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

lessons.situation: Sophie shares the HR calendar: reviews, holidays, and team birthdays.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Meses: January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December.

💛 Meses sempre com letra maiúscula! E use in para mês, on para data.

grammarDeepDive.title: Months and dates — in, on
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Os 12 meses em inglês começam sempre com letra maiúscula.

Para falar de mês, use in: in January, in December.
Para falar de data específica, use on: on July 10, on the 10th of July.

Em inglês britânico, escreve-se 10 July 2026 ou 10th July. Em inglês americano: July 10, 2026.

💛 Lembre: in = mês; on = dia.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online reference.

lessons.title: Pedidos: Please and Thank You — Can + please
lessons.objective: Fazer pedidos educados no trabalho com can + please.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

At work, we often ask for help. The most polite way in English is with "can" and "please": Can you help me, please? Can I have the report, please? Small words, big impact.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

lessons.situation: Sophie and colleagues exchange polite requests during the workday.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Pedidos educados com can:
• Can you + verbo + please? → Can you help me, please?
• Can I + verbo + please? → Can I have the report, please?

"Please" pode vir no início ou no fim: Please, help me. / Help me, please.

💛 Regra de ouro: toda vez que pedir, acrescente please. Nunca falha.

grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Para pedir algo educadamente em inglês:
• Can you/I + verbo + please? → nível educado.
• Could you/I + verbo + please? → ainda mais formal.
• Would you mind + -ing? → super formal.

"Please" pode aparecer no início, no meio ou no fim. O importante é usá-lo.

💛 Quanto mais palavras, mais educado. "Could you possibly help me, please?" soa muito cortês.

Our teams are made of people — and people have qualities. Today we learn 5 adjectives that describe great colleagues: kind, smart, helpful, friendly, reliable.

Em inglês, adjetivos vêm antes do substantivo ou depois do verbo to be:

lessons.grammar: was / were — past simple of to be
lessons.objective: Falar sobre hoje e ontem usando was e were.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Today we are at work; yesterday we were too. In English, the past of "am/is" is "was", and the past of "are" is "were". Two short words unlock the past.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

The meeting was great.

lessons.situation: Sophie and colleagues talk about yesterday's meeting and today's plans.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Past simple of to be:
• I / he / she / it → was
• you / we / they → were

Exemplos:
• I was at the office yesterday.
• We were in a meeting.
• She was tired.

💛 Regra direta: I/he/she/it → was; you/we/they → were.

💛 O passado é a base para contar qualquer história.

lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Tomorrow is another day at Czarnikow. To talk about the future, English uses "will + verb". I will help, she will call, we will meet. It's that simple!

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

lessons.grammarDetail:
Simple Future com will:
• I / you / he / she / it / we / they + will + verbo (infinitivo sem to).
• I will help. / She will call.

Contração comum: I'll, she'll, we'll.
Negativa: won't = will not.

💛 Will funciona igual para todas as pessoas — sem -s, sem mudança. Fácil e poderoso.

lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

💛 Parabéns — 20 lições! Today we look back at your first month at Czarnikow. We will use Simple Past regular verbs (worked, helped, started) to tell the story of a great beginning.

Today you will learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

lessons.grammarDetail:
Simple Past — verbos regulares:
• Adicione -ed: work → worked, learn → learned, help → helped.
• Se termina em -e: start → started, arrive → arrived.

Alguns verbos são irregulares: meet → met, have → had, go → went.

💛 Comece pelos regulares (+ed) e acrescente os irregulares aos poucos. Paciência vira fluência!

grammarDeepDive.title: Simple Past — regular verbs
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Para formar o Simple Past de verbos regulares, adicionamos -ed:
• work → worked
• help → helped
• learn → learned
• start → started (já termina em -t, ganha só -ed)
• arrive → arrived (termina em -e, ganha só -d)

Verbos irregulares têm formas próprias: meet → met, have → had, go → went, be → was/were.

💛 Celebrar cada palavra aprendida é parte do processo. Well done!
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online reference.

grammarDeepDive.title: The verb "to be" in IT sentences
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
No mundo de TI, o verbo to be aparece o tempo todo: The system is slow. The users are online. I am in the network.

Lembre: am só com I; is com he, she, it e coisas no singular (the computer, the data, the system); are com you, we, they e coisas no plural (the users, the computers).

💛 Dica: em inglês, data é tratado como singular na fala do dia a dia: The data is safe.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online reference.

grammarDeepDive.title: Possessives: my and your
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
My = meu, minha, meus, minhas (do falante).
Your = seu, sua, seus, suas (da pessoa com quem você fala).

Em inglês, o possessivo vem antes do substantivo: my laptop, your keyboard. Não muda com o plural: my laptops, your keyboards.

💛 Dica: não confunda your (possessivo) com you're (you are).

grammarDeepDive.title: "There is" and "there are"
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Use there is (há / existe) + substantivo no singular.
Use there are (há / existem) + substantivo no plural.

Ex.: There is a mouse. There are two monitors.

Na negativa: There isn't / There aren't. Na pergunta: Is there…? Are there…?

💛 Dica: em conversa, usa-se muito a contração there's para there is.

grammarDeepDive.title: Regular plurals in English

A maioria dos substantivos em inglês forma o plural com -s: app → apps, program → programs, file → files.

💛 Dica: o imperativo é direto, mas please faz toda a diferença no tom.

grammarDeepDive.title: Adjectives: describing things simply
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Em inglês, os adjetivos são simples:

• Vêm antes do substantivo: a slow laptop, a broken mouse.

grammarDeepDive.title: Countable nouns: a, an, some
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Substantivos contáveis podem ser contados (1, 2, 3 folders).

• a — antes de palavra começando em consoante: a folder, a file.
• an — antes de palavra começando em vogal ou som vocálico: an email, an issue, an urgent case.
• some — plural ou sem quantidade definida: some files, some documents.

💛 Dica: a regra é pelo som, não pela letra: an hour (h mudo), a user (som de "iu").

• He — homem: James → He
• She — mulher: Maria → She
• It — coisa/animal/sistema: the laptop → It
• They — plural (pessoas ou coisas): James and Maria → They

💛 Dica: para falar do time sem saber o gênero, they também pode ser usado no singular no inglês moderno.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online reference.

grammarDeepDive.title: Describing connection quality
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Os pares mais comuns:

• fast ↔ slow — velocidade
• strong ↔ weak — força do sinal
• stable ↔ unstable — estabilidade

Use very para intensificar: very fast, very weak.
Use too para algo excessivo: too slow (lento demais).

💛 Dica: em reuniões, diga my connection is unstable today para se justificar educadamente.

grammarDeepDive.title: Basic comparatives
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Para comparar duas coisas em inglês, use adjetivo + -er + than:
• fast → faster than
• big → bigger than (duplica a consoante)
• small → smaller than
• light → lighter than

Adjetivos longos usam more: more expensive, more powerful.

💛 Dica: o padrão básico é A is ___er than B.

Should é um verbo modal usado para dar conselhos:

💛 Dica: should é mais suave que must. Use should para conselhos, must para obrigações.

lessons.title: What Is a Supply Chain? — As Primeiras Palavras
lessons.grammar: Verbo to be — am, is, are
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras essenciais de supply chain e usá-las com o verbo to be.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

A supply chain is the path of a product from the farm or factory to the final customer. It is a chain of steps: produce, move, store, deliver. At Czarnikow, the supply chain carries sugar, coffee and other products around the world.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Verb to be (am / is / are). We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: A supply chain connects every farm, factory and port to our final customer.
The sugar comes from a supplier in the interior of São Paulo.
Our main customer in Europe buys 10,000 tonnes a year.
The factory in Brazil packs sugar for both domestic and export markets.
The product arrives at the port after seven days on the road.

lessons.situation: Maria explains the supply chain to a new colleague. She speaks slowly and uses very short sentences.
lessons.grammarDetail:
O verbo to be (ser / estar).
Use to be para dizer quem você é e onde algo está.

I am — Eu sou / estou
You are — Você é / está
He / She / It is — Ele / Ela é / está
We / You / They are — Nós / Vocês / Eles são / estão

💛 Calma, cada frase é uma vitória!

grammarDeepDive.title: The verb "to be" — o primeiro passo do inglês
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
O verbo to be é o alicerce do inglês. Ele diz quem somos, onde estamos e como algo é. Em português temos ser e estar; em inglês é só to be.

• am — só com I
• is — com he, she, it e nomes singulares
• are — com you, we, they e nomes plurais

💛 Comece com a forma completa. Contrações (I'm, it's, we're) vêm depois.

lessons.grammar: Sequence words — first, then, next, after, finally
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras de etapas e usar palavras de sequência para descrever processos.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

A product travels from the farm to the customer in clear steps. First, the farmer grows the sugar. Then, a truck moves it to the factory. Next, workers pack it. After that, a ship carries it. Finally, the customer receives the product.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Sequence words. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: First, the farmer harvests the sugarcane in the fields.
Then the truck takes the cane to the mill for processing.
Next, the mill turns it into white or raw sugar.
After that, the bags are stored in a large warehouse.
Finally, the sugar is loaded onto the ship at Santos.

lessons.situation: Carlos, a new intern, asks how sugar moves from the farm to the customer. You explain in simple steps.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Palavras de sequência.
Use estas palavras para organizar uma ideia:

First — primeiro
Then / Next — depois / em seguida
After that — depois disso
Finally — finalmente

💛 Passo a passo sempre chega longe.

A warehouse is a big building where we store products. There are shelves, boxes and pallets. There is a forklift to move heavy things. There is always a team of workers.

grammarDeepDive.title: There is / there are — descrevendo espaços

lessons.title: Boxes and Pallets — Contáveis e Incontáveis
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras ligadas a embalagem e diferenciar substantivos contáveis e incontáveis.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

In the warehouse we count boxes and pallets. But we cannot count sugar or coffee one by one — we measure them. Some words are countable (one box, two boxes). Other words are uncountable (some sugar, a lot of coffee).

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Countable and uncountable nouns. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: There are twelve boxes on each pallet, ready for the truck.
A pallet holds forty bags of twenty-five kilos each.
Sugar is uncountable — we measure it in tonnes.
Rice is uncountable in English — "some rice," never "a rice."
We count boxes, we measure sugar.

lessons.situation: You help a new employee label boxes and pallets in the warehouse. You explain what we count and what we measure.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Contáveis e incontáveis.
Contáveis: podemos contar (one box, two boxes). Plural existe.
Incontáveis: não contamos unidades (sugar, coffee, water). Sem plural.

Use a/an com contáveis no singular. Use some / a lot of com incontáveis.

💛 Dica: sugar é incontável, mas a bag of sugar é contável.

grammarDeepDive.title: Countable and uncountable nouns — contáveis e incontáveis
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Em inglês, substantivos se dividem em dois grupos:

• Contáveis (countable): têm singular e plural. a box / two boxes, one pallet / ten pallets.
• Incontáveis (uncountable): não têm plural. sugar, coffee, water, information, tape.

Com contáveis singulares, use a ou an. Com incontáveis, use some, any, a lot of.

💛 Um truque: para tornar um incontável "contável", use uma unidade — a bag of sugar, a cup of coffee, a bottle of water.

lessons.title: Trucks and Ships — Como o Produto Viaja
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras de transporte e usar a expressão by + meio de transporte.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Products travel by truck, by ship, by train or by plane. The choice depends on the distance and the urgency. At Czarnikow, sugar travels by truck to the port and by ship across the ocean.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise By + transport. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: The cargo travels by truck from the mill to the port.
From Santos, the ship sails by sea to Rotterdam.
Urgent samples go by plane to our London office.
In the UK, many deliveries arrive by train from the ports.
A container holds about 22 tonnes of sugar in bags.

lessons.situation: A colleague asks you how sugar reaches customers in Europe. You explain each transport mode using "by".
lessons.grammarDetail:
By + meio de transporte.
Use by (sem the) antes do meio de transporte.

• by truck (de caminhão)
• by ship (de navio)
• by train (de trem)
• by plane / by air (de avião)

Atenção: on foot — a pé. Exceção à regra.

💛 Sem "the": we travel by truck, not by the truck.

takeaways: Products travel by truck, by ship, by train or by plane.

grammarDeepDive.title: By + transport — como dizer o meio de transporte
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Para dizer o meio de transporte, use by + substantivo (sem artigo):

by truck, by ship, by train, by plane, by bus, by car, by bike.

Exceção: on foot (a pé).

Se você quer ser específico (meu carro, o navio x), use outra estrutura: in my car, on the ship "MV Atlas".

💛 Para supply chain, a combinação mais comum é: by truck, by ship, by rail, by air.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entry for reference.

lessons.title: Orders and Deliveries — Pedidos Todo Dia
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras sobre pedidos e usar o Present Simple para rotinas.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Every day we receive orders from customers. We check stock, prepare the delivery and send the truck. This is the daily routine of a supply chain team.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Present Simple. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: We receive orders every morning, Monday to Friday.
The system confirms each delivery automatically.
Our customer usually places an order one week in advance.
The invoice is sent the same day the truck leaves.
Delivery times depend on distance, weather and port traffic.

lessons.situation: A new team member shadows you for a day. You describe your routine using Present Simple.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Present Simple.
Usado para rotinas e fatos.

I / you / we / they → verbo sem s (I work, we check)
He / she / it → verbo com s (he works, she checks)

💛 No passado ficamos com medo do "s". No presente ele é seu amigo!

grammarDeepDive.title: Present Simple — a rotina do inglês
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
O Present Simple é o tempo da rotina. Use para falar de coisas que acontecem sempre, todos os dias, como hábito.

Regra principal: com he, she, it, o verbo recebe -s.

• I check / you check / we check / they check
• He checks / she checks / it checks

Verbos terminados em -o, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x recebem -es: goes, watches, finishes, passes.

💛 Não esqueça do "s" no he/she/it. Ele é pequeno, mas muda tudo.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entry for reference.

lessons.title: Suppliers and Buyers — Quem é Quem
lessons.grammar: Subject pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they)
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras sobre parceiros comerciais e usar os pronomes pessoais do sujeito.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

A supplier is a company that sells to us. A buyer is a company that buys from us. Together, suppliers and buyers make the supply chain work.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Subject pronouns. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: The supplier is the mill that produces our raw sugar.
The buyer is the company that purchases the product.
A broker like Czarnikow connects supplier and buyer.
The client expects clear, fast communication at every step.
The producer decides how much sugar goes to export this month.

lessons.situation: You present the main suppliers and buyers to a new colleague. You use pronouns to make your speech shorter.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Pronomes pessoais do sujeito.

I — Eu
You — Você / Vocês
He — Ele
She — Ela
It — Ele/Ela (coisa/animal)
We — Nós
They — Eles/Elas

💛 Use pronomes para não repetir os nomes toda hora.

grammarDeepDive.title: Subject pronouns — os pronomes do sujeito
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Os pronomes de sujeito substituem nomes e evitam repetição. Em inglês, são sete:

I, you, he, she, it, we, they.

Cuidado com o it: usamos para coisas, animais e situações (The contract is ready. It is here.).

O you serve para singular e plural — muda conforme o contexto.

💛 Comece sempre a frase com o pronome em maiúscula: I é sempre grande!

Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.

lessons.title: Stock In and Out — Entrando e Saindo
lessons.grammar: Prepositions of movement (in, out, into, from, to)
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras de movimentação de estoque e usar preposições básicas.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Products come into the warehouse and go out to the customer. Stock moves from the truck to the shelf. Every movement is registered.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Prepositions of movement. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: New stock comes in from the mill every Tuesday.
Finished pallets go out of the warehouse by the afternoon.
The forklift moves boxes into the truck, one layer at a time.
Sugar travels from the port to the customer's warehouse.
Empty pallets come back from the client for reuse.

lessons.situation: You train a new employee on stock movements. You use in, out, into, from, to.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Preposições de movimento.

• in / into — para dentro
• out / out of — para fora
• from — de (origem)
• to — para (destino)
• on — sobre (superfície)

💛 Aponte com o dedo enquanto fala: in, out, from, to.

lessons.wrapup: 💛 Você aprendeu 5 palavras novas e prepositions of movement. Isso é uma vitória! Pratique 5 minutos amanhã.
takeaways: Stock goes in and stock goes out.
Use into for entering, out of for leaving.
From marks the origin.
To marks the destination.
Every movement is a record.

Prepositions are small but powerful.

grammarDeepDive.title: Prepositions of movement — as direções
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Preposições de movimento mostram a direção de algo.

• in / into — entrar (Put the box into the warehouse.)
• out of — sair (Take the pallet out of the truck.)
• from — origem (The sugar comes from Brazil.)
• to — destino (The order goes to Germany.)
• on — superfície (The label is on the box.)

💛 Dica: use into/out of quando há movimento claro. Use in/out sozinhos quando já há contexto.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entry for reference.

lessons.title: The Delivery Day — Dias e Horas
lessons.grammar: Days of the week + time expressions (on Monday, at 9 am)
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras sobre entrega e dizer corretamente dias e horários em inglês.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Every delivery has a day and a time. We say "on Monday" for days and "at 9 am" for hours. Planning the delivery day is a key part of supply chain.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Days of the week and time expressions. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: Our main delivery day is Wednesday, at 9 in the morning.
On Fridays, the warehouse closes at 4 pm.
The ship arrives in Rotterdam on Monday.
Deliveries to the UK happen on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
Meetings with Santos are at 2 pm, London time.

lessons.situation: You plan the week of deliveries with your team. You name days and hours correctly.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Dias e horas.

• on + dia da semana → on Monday, on Friday
• at + hora → at 9 am, at 3 pm
• in + parte do dia → in the morning, in the afternoon

Note: at night (com at, não in).

💛 On dia, at hora. Memorize: on Friday at 9 am.

grammarDeepDive.title: Days and times — on, at, in
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Três preposições, três usos:

• on — dias e datas: on Monday, on 5 May
• at — horas e momentos: at 9 am, at night, at noon
• in — partes do dia, meses, estações, anos: in the morning, in July, in 2024

Uma frase completa: The meeting is on Monday at 10 in the morning.

💛 Memorize essa frase — ela cobre 90% dos casos.

Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.

lessons.title: Quantities — Os Números do Estoque
lessons.grammar: Numbers and quantifiers (many, a lot of, some, a few)
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras sobre quantidades e usar quantificadores comuns.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

In supply chain, numbers are everywhere. We have 200 bags, a lot of boxes and a few pallets. Quantifiers help us describe without being too exact.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Numbers and quantifiers. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: The total amount of sugar in stock today is 480 tonnes.
The total for the month is 12,000 bags shipped.
Each unit weighs exactly 25 kilograms.
We have many boxes, but only a few empty pallets.
A little more tape, and we're ready to close the pallet.

lessons.situation: You do a stock count with a new team member. You use quantifiers and numbers.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Quantifiers.

• many — muitos (contáveis)
• much — muito (incontáveis) — em frases negativas
• a lot of — muitos/muito (ambos)
• some — alguns
• a few — poucos
• a little — um pouco (incontáveis)

💛 Em dúvida? a lot of serve em quase tudo.

grammarDeepDive.title: Quantifiers — quantidades no dia a dia
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Os quantifiers dizem "quanto" sem dar um número exato.

• many → contáveis plural (many boxes)
• much → incontáveis, em negativas/perguntas (not much sugar, how much sugar?)
• a lot of → ambos (a lot of boxes, a lot of sugar)
• some → ambos, em afirmativas (some boxes, some sugar)
• a few → contáveis (a few pallets)
• a little → incontáveis (a little tape)

💛 Dica: a few e a little têm sentido positivo (tem um pouco). few e little sem "a" têm sentido negativo (quase nada).
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entry for reference.

lessons.title: A Simple Invoice — Fatura Básica
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras ligadas a faturamento e usar have / has.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

An invoice is a document with the price, the amount and the buyer. Every delivery has an invoice. Every company has a tax number.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Have / has. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: The invoice has the client's name, the product and the total price.
Our client has 30 days to pay after the invoice is issued.
Every order has a unique number for tracking.
The seller has the responsibility to deliver on time.
The buyer has the right to check every shipment on arrival.

lessons.situation: You help a colleague read an invoice. You use have and has to describe its parts.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Have / has.

I / you / we / they → have
He / she / it → has

Use para posse e características.
I have an invoice. She has a question. The invoice has a number.

💛 Com she/he/it → has. Sempre.

grammarDeepDive.title: Have and has — posse e características

lessons.title: Problems in the Chain — Adjetivos Úteis
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras sobre problemas e usar adjetivos em frases simples.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Sometimes problems happen. A delivery is late. A box is broken. A price is high. A customer is unhappy. Adjectives describe these situations.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Adjectives. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: A late delivery creates a tough conversation with the client.
A damaged pallet means extra paperwork and a replacement.
A slow port can delay the whole shipment by days.
A strong team responds to problems quickly and calmly.
A clear invoice avoids half the problems in the chain.

lessons.situation: A customer reports a problem. You use adjectives to describe the situation honestly.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Adjetivos.

Em inglês, o adjetivo vem antes do substantivo:
a late delivery, a broken box.

Ou depois do verbo to be:
The delivery is late. The box is broken.

💛 Adjetivos em inglês não têm plural: late deliveries, nunca lates deliveries.

grammarDeepDive.title: Adjectives — como descrever
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Adjetivos descrevem pessoas, coisas e situações.

Em inglês, duas posições principais:

• Antes do substantivo: a late delivery, a broken box, a wrong price.
• Depois do verbo to be: The delivery is late. The box is broken.

Regra de ouro: adjetivos em inglês não têm forma plural: late deliveries (e não "lates").

💛 No português falamos "entregas atrasadas"; no inglês é "late deliveries" — o "s" fica só no substantivo.

lessons.title: Tracking a Shipment — Onde Está o Pedido?
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras sobre rastreamento e fazer perguntas com where.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

When a shipment is on the way, everybody asks: where is it? Tracking gives the answer. Every shipment has a number, a map and a status.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Questions with where. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: Where is the shipment right now — in Santos or at sea?
Where are the missing boxes from last week's order?
The tracking number is on the top right of the invoice.
Our system shows every truck in real time.
The ETA is updated every four hours during the voyage.

lessons.situation: A customer calls to ask where the shipment is. You check the tracking and answer.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Where is / where are.

Where is + singular → Where is the truck?
Where are + plural → Where are the pallets?

Responda com in, at, near, on the way.

💛 Where começa quase toda conversa sobre tracking.

Para perguntar sobre localização, use where + verbo to be:

• Where are + sujeito plural → Where are the pallets?

Para responder, use preposições de lugar: in (dentro de um lugar grande), at (ponto específico), on (superfície).

💛 Essa estrutura cobre 80% das perguntas em supply chain.

lessons.title: Coffee, Sugar, Cocoa — Nossos Produtos
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 nomes de produtos da Czarnikow e usar substantivos incontáveis em contexto.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

At Czarnikow we trade sugar, coffee, ethanol and cocoa. These products are uncountable: we measure them in tonnes, not in pieces. We buy, store and deliver around the world.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Product names and uncountables. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: Sugar is our main product — over two million tonnes a year.
Coffee is another big product at Czarnikow.
Cocoa is uncountable — "some cocoa," never "a cocoa."
All three are soft commodities: sugar, coffee, cocoa.
The weight of each container depends on the product.

lessons.situation: You introduce Czarnikow's products to a new colleague. You use uncountable nouns correctly.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Nomes de produtos.
Estes substantivos são uncountable: sem plural, sem a/an.

Certo: some sugar, a lot of coffee, 200 tonnes of cocoa.
Errado: a sugar, two coffees (para grão).

💛 Em inglês, a coffee existe, mas significa "um cafezinho" — não o grão.

grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Os produtos que a Czarnikow negocia são, na maioria, incontáveis. Isso muda três coisas:

1. Sem plural (não existe sugars no sentido de "açúcares").
2. Sem artigo a/an.
3. Use quantificadores como some, a lot of, tonnes of, kilos of.

Exceção: em contexto de bebida, coffee e tea viram contáveis (Two coffees, please.).

💛 Em supply chain, a pergunta é sempre "quanto": how much sugar? how many tonnes?

lessons.title: Weights and Measures — Pesando o Mundo
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras de peso e medida e usar números com unidades.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

We measure our products in kilos, bags and tonnes. One bag weighs 50 kilos. One tonne equals 1,000 kilos. A ship can carry 50,000 tonnes of sugar.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Measurements. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: A tonne is one thousand kilos — our standard unit for sugar.
Each bag weighs either 25 or 50 kilos, depending on the market.
A container holds about 22 tonnes of bagged sugar.
The weight note shows the exact kilos at loading.
Measurement errors can cost thousands of dollars per shipment.

lessons.situation: You weigh a shipment and describe the result in kilos and tonnes.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Números + unidades.

50 kilos, 1,000 tonnes, 20 bags.

Use weighs (pesa) e equals (equivale a):
The bag weighs 50 kilos. One tonne equals 1,000 kilos.

💛 Atenção: tonne (tonelada métrica) ≠ ton (tonelada americana).

grammarDeepDive.title: Measurements — números e unidades
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Para medir, combine um número com uma unidade:

50 kilos, 1,000 tonnes, 25 bags.

Em inglês, usamos weigh(s) (pesar) como verbo: The bag weighs 50 kilos.

E equal(s) para equivalência: One tonne equals 1,000 kilos.

Diferença importante:
• tonne (métrico) = 1,000 kilos.
• ton (EUA) = 907 kilos.
Em supply chain internacional, use tonne.

💛 Com números grandes, separe por vírgulas: 1,000 / 50,000.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entry for reference.

lessons.title: Time to Arrive — Chegadas e Horários
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras sobre chegada e usar at + hora, arrive at/in.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Every truck and every ship arrives at a specific time and at a specific place. "Arrive at" is used for buildings and points. "Arrive in" is used for cities and countries.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Time and arrivals. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: The truck arrives at the warehouse at 9 am.
The ship arrives in Rotterdam on Tuesday morning.
The train arrives in London at half past two.
The plane arrives in Heathrow at 6:45 London time.
The client arrives at reception fifteen minutes early.

lessons.situation: You update a customer about arrivals. You use arrive at / in + times.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Arrive at / in.

• arrive at + lugar específico (aeroporto, porto, prédio)
• arrive in + cidade, país

Exemplos:
The truck arrives at the port. The ship arrives in Rotterdam.

💛 Nunca "arrive to" — é um erro comum.

grammarDeepDive.title: Arrive at / in — a chegada certa
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Uma das diferenças mais importantes em inglês:

• arrive at + lugar específico (at the port, at the office, at the airport).
• arrive in + cidade, país, região (in Rotterdam, in Brazil).

Para horários, use at: arrive at 9 am.
Para dias, use on: arrive on Monday.

💛 Erro clássico: arrive to. Não use "to" depois de "arrive". Nunca.

Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.

lessons.title: Planning the Week — Going to
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras sobre planejamento e usar going to para planos.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Every Monday we plan the week. We are going to send two ships, check the stock and meet a new supplier. "Going to" shows decisions made before the moment of speaking.

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Future with going to. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: I'm going to visit the Santos mill next Monday.
We're going to plan the October shipments this afternoon.
The client is going to send the forecast by Friday.
James is going to join the Wednesday call from London.
The team is going to review last month's delays tomorrow.

lessons.situation: You lead the weekly planning meeting. You announce plans using going to.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Going to.
Use para planos e intenções.

Estrutura: subject + am/is/are + going to + verb.
I am going to send the report. She is going to meet the supplier. We are going to close the gate at 6.

💛 "Going to" é como "vou" em português.

grammarDeepDive.title: Going to — falando de planos
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Going to é a forma mais comum de falar de planos no futuro próximo.

Estrutura: sujeito + to be + going to + verbo no infinitivo.

• I am going to send the report.
• She is going to meet the supplier.
• We are going to close at 6.

Para negar: I am not going to work late.
Para perguntar: Are you going to send the email?

💛 Use "going to" quando o plano já existe. Use "will" quando decide na hora.

lessons.title: Yesterday's Delivery — Was / Were
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 palavras sobre ontem e usar was / were no passado.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Yesterday the delivery was on time. The pallets were ready. The customers were happy. "Was" and "were" are the past of "to be".

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Was / were. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: Yesterday's delivery was on time, for once.
The trucks were all loaded by nine in the morning.
The port was very busy last week because of the rain.
Our numbers were a little below target in September.
The team was fantastic during the peak season.

lessons.situation: You report yesterday's delivery to your manager using was / were.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Was / were.

I, he, she, it → was
You, we, they → were

Negativa: was not (wasn't) / were not (weren't).

💛 Was e were são o passado do verbo to be.

grammarDeepDive.title: Was / were — o passado do to be
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
O passado do verbo to be tem duas formas:

• was → I, he, she, it
• were → you, we, they

Exemplos:
I was at the office. She was tired. We were ready.

Negação:
I was not (wasn't) happy. They were not (weren't) on time.

Perguntas:
Was she at the meeting? Were you on time?

💛 Marcadores de tempo comuns: yesterday, last week, last month, two days ago.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entry for reference.

lessons.title: Thank You, Supplier — Frases Educadas
lessons.grammar: Polite phrases (please, thank you, could you)
lessons.objective: Aprender 5 frases educadas úteis e usá-las em pedidos profissionais.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Good business is polite business. "Please" and "thank you" are small words with big effect. "Could you" is softer than "can you".

Today you will learn 5 important words and practise Polite phrases. We start slow. You can do it!

vocab.example: Thank you to every supplier who delivered on time this month.
Could you please confirm the arrival by 5 pm today?
We really appreciate your flexibility with the last-minute change.
Please find attached the signed delivery note.

lessons.situation: You write a short email to a supplier using polite phrases.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Frases educadas.

• Could you…? — mais educado que can you…?
• Please no começo ou no fim.
• Thank you for + -ing: thank you for sending.
• I appreciate…: I appreciate your help.
• Best regards: fecho formal.

💛 Em inglês de negócios, educação abre portas.

grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Em inglês profissional, educação não é luxo — é ferramenta.

• Thank you — após qualquer ajuda.

• I appreciate… — versão mais formal.
• Best regards / Kind regards — fecho padrão.

💛 Quanto mais você pede algo difícil, mais educado precisa ser. É matemática.

lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Welcome to London, the home of Czarnikow since 1861. In this first lesson you'll meet the words you hear the moment you step off the plane at Heathrow — and the little verb to be that holds every English sentence together. Take your time. Confidence is built one word at a time.

vocab.example: London is the capital of the United Kingdom.
Our UK office is in central London, near the Thames.

lessons.objective: Aprender 5 cumprimentos e responder a perguntas básicas sobre como você está.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

British people greet each other dozens of times a day — in the lift, in the corridor, on the phone. None of it is complicated, but the right small word at the right moment makes you sound natural from day one. Let's practise the basics Sophie uses every morning in the London office.

vocab.example: "Hello!" is the safest greeting in a UK office.
In the UK, people say "Good morning" until about noon.
"I'm fine, thanks" is a polite, neutral answer at work.
We say "thank you" far more often than in Brazil.
"Nice to meet you" is the standard handshake line in London.

lessons.objective: Aprender 5 adjetivos para descrever pessoas e usar corretamente com o verbo to be.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

British business culture runs on small, polite adjectives. "Lovely," "quite good," "a bit busy" — these tiny words say a lot. Today we practise simple adjectives so you can describe people, meetings, and your day the way a Londoner would.

vocab.example: British people are generally polite, even when they disagree.
A "quiet" office doesn't mean people are unfriendly.
"Sorry" is used a hundred times a day in London.
British humour is often dry and understated.
A "lovely" email is a warm but professional email.

lessons.title: Thank You and Please — Londres para iniciantes
lessons.objective: Usar please e thank you com naturalidade em situações simples do dia a dia.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

In London you'll hear "please," "thank you" and "sorry" more times in one day than in a whole week in Brazil. These three little words are the engine of British politeness — and your quickest way to sound natural at work.

vocab.example: "Please" turns an order into a polite request.
"Thank you" is expected even for very small favours.
"Sorry" works for both apology and a gentle "excuse me."
"Excuse me" gets someone's attention without being rude.
"You're welcome" is the natural reply to thanks.

lessons.situation: Um funcionário pede ajuda a um colega britânico. Ele usa please e thank you em cada frase.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Please and thank you — o coração da polidez britânica
Na cultura britânica, please e thank you são usados o tempo todo — mesmo em pedidos pequenos. Omitir estas palavras pode soar rude.

💛 Sem medo de errar. Cada erro é uma aula grátis!

takeaways: "Please" softens every request.
"Thank you" is never too much in the UK.
"Sorry" can mean excuse me, pardon, or apology.
"Excuse me" opens a polite interruption.
"You're welcome" answers "thank you."
"Cheers" = informal thanks.
"Thanks a lot" is warmer than "thanks."
"No worries" replies to a small sorry.
Tone of voice matters as much as the words.
Politeness is the fastest door-opener in London.

lessons.title: Tea Time — Londres para iniciantes
lessons.objective: Usar o presente simples para falar de rotinas britânicas como o chá da tarde.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Tea isn't just a drink in the UK — it's a routine, a social ritual, and often where real conversations happen. Today we use the Present Simple to describe these everyday habits. Every office has them; yours will have its own soon.

vocab.example: British people drink tea several times a day at the office.
There's always milk in the fridge for the 11 o'clock break.
A biscuit with your tea is almost obligatory.
The small kitchen has a kettle ready at all times.
Our "tea break" is actually when most deals are discussed.

lessons.situation: No escritório, colegas fazem uma pausa para o chá da tarde. Falam sobre seus hábitos usando o presente simples.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Present Simple — hábitos e rotinas
Use o presente simples para falar de hábitos (I drink tea every day). Na terceira pessoa (he, she, it), o verbo termina em -s: she drinks tea.

💛 Sem medo de errar. Cada erro é uma aula grátis!

lessons.title: The Weather — Londres para iniciantes
lessons.objective: Falar sobre o clima usando it is + adjetivo, um dos assuntos preferidos dos britânicos.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Talking about the weather is not a cliché in the UK — it's a survival skill. It's how you break the ice in a lift, start a meeting, or fill a quiet moment. Today you'll learn the structure It is + weather and the vocabulary that keeps any small talk flowing.

vocab.example: It's raining in London — nothing unusual.
"It's a bit chilly" is British code for "very cold."
The weather is the default small-talk opener in the UK.
A sunny day in London is genuinely celebrated.
Always keep an umbrella in your bag — just in case.

lessons.grammarDetail:
Talking about the weather — o clássico small talk britânico
Para falar do clima, use it is + adjetivo (it is cold, it is sunny). Também é comum dizer: it is raining, it is snowing.

lessons.title: Underground and Buses — Londres para iniciantes
lessons.objective: Falar sobre como você vai para o trabalho usando by + transporte.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

London runs on public transport. Tube, bus, train, black cab — each has its own rules and its own rhythm. Today you'll learn the structure by + transport, which is the shortest way in English to say how you get anywhere.

vocab.example: Most Londoners travel by Underground, not by car.
By bus, you see more of the city — but you arrive later.
The Czarnikow office is a two-minute walk from the Tube station.
Clients often travel by train from outside London.
A black cab is useful when you're carrying sugar samples.

lessons.situation: Um colega explica ao visitante brasileiro como se locomover em Londres — tube, bus e taxi.
lessons.grammarDetail:
By + transport — como você viaja
Use by + meio de transporte (by tube, by bus, by train, by car). Exceção: on foot (a pé). Não use artigo: by the tube é errado.

💛 Sem medo de errar. Cada erro é uma aula grátis!

lessons.title: Shops in London — Londres para iniciantes
lessons.grammar: Preposições de lugar (in, on, next to)
lessons.objective: Localizar lojas e lugares usando preposições simples de lugar.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

London is a city of small shops tucked between big buildings. Being able to say where something is — next to, across from, opposite, on the corner — saves time every single day, from lunch to meetings to post-work pints.

vocab.example: The bakery is on the corner, next to the Tube station.
There's a good café in our building, on the ground floor.
The supermarket is open until late, just across the street.
The chemist (pharmacy) is at the end of the road.
The pub is right opposite the office — very handy after 5.

lessons.situation: Um turista pergunta a Sophie onde encontrar algumas lojas famosas de Londres. Ela responde com preposições claras.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Prepositions of place — onde as coisas estão
Preposições comuns: in (dentro), on (sobre/na rua), next to (ao lado), near (perto), between (entre). Use on para ruas (on Oxford Street).

💛 Sem medo de errar. Cada erro é uma aula grátis!

lessons.objective: Falar sobre o que você gosta de fazer usando like + verbo no gerúndio.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Small talk looks easy — but done well, it opens doors. Today you'll practise the structure like + -ing, the simplest way to talk about hobbies, weekends and everyday preferences in any London meeting.

vocab.example: Small talk is the warm-up before any British meeting.
The weather is the safest topic at any level.
Weekends are a popular small-talk subject on Monday.
Football works if you know your client's team.
Avoid politics and religion — keep it light.

lessons.situation: Dois colegas conversam no corredor sobre hobbies e planos de fim de semana — small talk clássico.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Like / love / enjoy + -ing — falando de hábitos
Após like, love, enjoy, hate, usamos o verbo com -ing: I like reading. I love walking. Ela não muda com o sujeito.

lessons.objective: Falar sobre as refeições do dia e o que você come.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Food vocabulary is part of office survival. Lunch meetings, client dinners, quick coffees — each one has its own little script. Today we'll cover the words you'll use every single day at work in London.

vocab.example: Breakfast in the office is usually coffee and a pastry.
Lunch is a quick sandwich between calls.
Dinner with a client is a chance to talk beyond the market.
A "full English" is a famous British breakfast.
Fish and chips is the classic London takeaway dinner.

lessons.situation: Sophie fala sobre refeições típicas britânicas — do English breakfast ao fish and chips.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Meals — refeições do dia em inglês britânico
Usamos have para refeições: have breakfast, have lunch, have dinner — sem artigo. Exemplo: I have lunch at one.

💛 Sem medo de errar. Cada erro é uma aula grátis!

lessons.title: Time in the UK — Londres para iniciantes
lessons.objective: Dizer as horas em inglês britânico usando at + horário.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Time in business English is crisp and precise. "At 9 am," "at half past two," "quarter to five" — these structures are used dozens of times a day in any London office. Let's get them second nature.

vocab.example: The market opens at 9 am sharp.
Our weekly call with Santos is at 2 pm London time.
Lunch is usually at 1 pm.
Clients appreciate a punctual 9 am.
The office closes at 6 pm, but emails continue later.

lessons.situation: Um colega marca uma reunião e explica como os britânicos falam de horários.
lessons.grammarDetail:
Telling the time — horas em inglês britânico
Para horas certas: it is three o'clock. Para 30: half past three. Para 15: quarter past / quarter to. Use at + horário: the meeting is at nine.

💛 Sem medo de errar. Cada erro é uma aula grátis!

lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

British culture has a few unwritten rules — and breaking them is noticed instantly. Today we'll practise must and should: the quickest way to describe a rule, a habit, or a piece of friendly advice.

vocab.example: You must queue — jumping a line is a serious offence in the UK.
You should say "please" and "thank you" constantly.
You mustn't push on the Tube, even when it's crowded.
You should hold the door for the person behind you.
You must respect quiet carriages on the train.

lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

The pub is an extension of the London office. Deals are celebrated there, Fridays end there, and colleagues become friends over a pint. Today we'll use have / has to order, describe and talk about the food, drinks and company you find in any good pub.

lessons.title: Sorry and Excuse Me — Londres para iniciantes
lessons.objective: Distinguir e usar corretamente sorry e excuse me em diferentes situações.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

If politeness is the British national sport, "sorry" and "excuse me" are its most-used plays. Today we'll master the small phrases that keep London's crowded offices, streets and Tubes running smoothly.

vocab.example: "Sorry" works when you bump into someone on the pavement.
"Excuse me" is how you politely ask a colleague for a minute.
"Pardon?" is the polite way to ask someone to repeat.
"My apologies" fits a late email or small mistake at work.
"No worries" is a warm reply to a small "sorry."

Sorry vs. Excuse me — duas frases, dois usos
Use excuse me para chamar atenção, passar ou interromper. Use sorry para pedir desculpas por algo já feito ou para pedir para repetir (Sorry? / Pardon?).

lessons.title: A London Weekend — Londres para iniciantes
lessons.objective: Falar de planos de fim de semana usando going to.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

Weekends in London are full of small, lovely plans — markets, walks, Sunday roasts. Today we use going to to talk about those plans. It's the easiest structure in English to sound confident about the future.

vocab.example: I'm going to visit the market on Saturday morning.
We're going to have brunch near the river on Sunday.
The team is going to meet for a pub roast.
Sophie is going to show me the British Museum.
I'm going to rest, honestly — London is busy!
