lessons.title: The British Accent — Londres para iniciantes
lessons.objective: Reconhecer características do sotaque britânico (RP) em frases simples.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

The British accent isn't one accent — it's dozens. RP, Cockney, Scouse, Geordie, Scottish, Welsh… even within the London office, you'll hear several. Today we'll practise listening patiently and asking politely for a repeat.

vocab.example: British accents vary — London alone has several.
The "Received Pronunciation" is the classic BBC accent.
Cockney is the traditional East London accent.
Many brokers drop the "t" in the middle of words.
Don't panic when you meet a strong accent — ask politely for a repeat.

lessons.situation: Sophie explica que o sotaque britânico (RP) é claro e pausado, e que pedir para repetir é perfeitamente educado.
lessons.grammarDetail:
British accent — um primeiro contato
No sotaque britânico (RP), o R final quase não é pronunciado (car soa como "cah") e os Ts são mais marcados. Para pedir para repetir, use: Sorry? Pardon? Could you repeat, please?.

💛 Sem medo de errar. Cada erro é uma aula grátis!

takeaways: There isn't one British accent.

lessons.title: An Email to a UK Colleague — Londres para iniciantes
lessons.objective: Escrever um email curto e educado a um colega britânico.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

A UK email is short, polite and clear. You don't need to write a speech — just the right opener, a clear body, and the correct sign-off. Today we'll walk through every piece so your next email to London lands exactly right.

vocab.example: "Dear James" is the standard formal opening.
"Hi Sophie" works with close colleagues.
"I hope this email finds you well" is the classic warm-up.
"Best regards" is the neutral, safe sign-off.
"Kind regards" is slightly warmer — great for clients.

lessons.grammarDetail:
Emails in British English — formal e educado
Abertura formal: Dear Sophie. Informal: Hi Sophie. Fechamento formal: Best regards / Kind regards. Informal: Best / Thanks.

lessons.objective: Revisar os principais cumprimentos, despedidas e frases educadas aprendidas no track.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma dica: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts.

A good ending matters as much as a good start. Today we wrap up the UK track with the phrases you'll use every single day to close meetings, emails, and conversations — and you'll review what you learned across the track.

vocab.example: "Goodbye" is a bit formal — "bye" is what most people say.
"See you soon" is friendly and keeps the door open.
"Take care" is warm without being too personal.
"Have a good one" is a very British informal closer.
"Cheerio!" is a classic, slightly old-fashioned farewell.

lessons.intro:

Accounting is the language of Czarnikow's numbers. Today's lesson — What Is Accounting? — gives you short, practical sentences you can use with the finance team.

Hoje você vai aprender 5 palavras úteis e praticar em frases curtas e naturais. Vá com calma — um passo de cada vez. You can do it!

The balance looks healthy after this week's payments.

grammarDeepDive.title: Prepositions of time — in, on, at
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
• in: meses, anos, partes do dia (in May, in 2026, in the morning).
• on: dias e datas (on Friday, on 10 April).
• at: horários e expressões fixas (at 9 a.m., at night, at the end of the month).
references: Murphy — English Grammar in Use, Unit 121: at / on / in (time).
Eastwood — Oxford Practice Grammar, Unit 223.
Cambridge Dictionary — "prepositions of time".

lessons.objective: Aprender a se apresentar no trabalho usando I am e you are.
lessons.intro:
💛 Cada "hi" é o começo de uma conversa.

Your first day at a new desk can feel big. A simple "Hi, I'm Ana, I work at Czarnikow" opens every door. Today we practise I am / you are with the people and places you see every day.

Today: 5 useful words and plenty of practice. Take your time — every sentence counts.

lessons.situation: Oliver uses simple sentences to practise to be (I am / you are) in a Czarnikow context. The language is slow, clear and supportive.
lessons.grammarDetail:
I am / You are.

You are my colleague. — Você é meu colega.

💛 Cada palavra nova é um passo à frente.

Substantivos contáveis têm plural e usam a/an: a sandwich, an apple.

💛 Coffee = bebida em geral; a coffee = uma xícara.

lessons.intro:
💛 Olhar para ontem ajuda a planejar amanhã.

Last week had its good moments and its busy ones. Today we use was and were to tell that story in simple past: Monday was busy, the calls were long, the team was great.

Today: 5 useful words and plenty of practice. Take your time — every sentence counts.

vocab.example: Yesterday was busy.
Last week was good.
Two days ago.
I was busy.
It was easy.

lessons.grammarDetail:

I/he/she/it was. You/we/they were.

lessons.objective: Responder emails curtos de forma clara.
lessons.intro:
💛 Uma resposta curta e clara vale por dez.

Short email replies save everyone time. A good one thanks, confirms, attaches and closes warmly. Today we collect the five phrases you'll reuse forever.

Today: 5 useful words and plenty of practice. Take your time — every sentence counts.

lessons.intro:

grammarDeepDive.title: The verb "to be" in trade — o ponto de partida
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
O verbo to be é a base do inglês de trade. Ele diz o que algo é, onde está e como está.

• am — com I
• is — com he, she, it e nomes singulares (the price, the market)
• are — com you, we, they e plurais (the goods, the markets)

💛 Dica: contrações como I'm, it's, we're soam naturais. Comece pela forma completa e vá soltando com o tempo.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entries.

grammarDeepDive.title: Personal pronouns — as peças básicas da frase
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Em inglês, o pronome vem quase sempre antes do verbo. Os principais são:

• I — eu
• You — você / vocês
• He — ele
• She — ela
• It — ele/ela (coisa, animal, empresa, mercado)
• We — nós
• They — eles / elas

💛 Dica: em inglês, it é muito usado — para o mercado, o preço, o contrato, a empresa. Não tenha medo dele!

grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Números em inglês seguem um padrão simples:

• 1–12 têm nomes próprios (one, two... twelve)
• 13–19 terminam em -teen (thirteen, fourteen...)
• 20, 30, 40... terminam em -ty (twenty, thirty...)
• Use hundred, thousand, million (sem s quando há número antes: two hundred, não two hundreds).

Moedas comuns em trade: USD (US dollar), GBP (British pound), EUR (euro), BRL (Brazilian real).

💛 Dica: no escritório, dizemos four hundred dollars per tonne, não four hundreds.

Comparativo em inglês:

• Adjetivo curto + -er: high → higher, low → lower, cheap → cheaper.
• Adjetivo longo: more + adjetivo: more expensive, more important.
• Irregulares: good → better, bad → worse.
• Usamos than para comparar: Higher than yesterday.

grammarDeepDive.title: Possessive adjectives — de quem é isso?
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Pronomes possessivos mostram de quem é algo:

• my — meu/minha
• your — seu/sua (para você e para vocês)
• his — dele
• her — dela
• its — dele/dela (coisa, empresa, animal)
• our — nosso(a)
• their — deles/delas

💛 Cuidado: its (possessivo) ≠ it's (= it is).

grammarDeepDive.title: Present Simple — a rotina do trader
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
O Present Simple é usado para rotinas e fatos.

• I / you / we / they + verbo simples: I work, you work, we work, they work.
• he / she / it + verbo + -s: He works, she checks, it opens.

Verbos terminados em -o, -ch, -sh, -ss ganham -es: he goes, she watches, it crashes.

💛 Dica: o grande vilão da terceira pessoa é esquecer o -s. Marque mentalmente: he/she/it → +s.

Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.

grammarDeepDive.title: Weight units — tonnes, kilos, bags, containers
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Unidades de peso em trade internacional:

• 1 tonne (MT) = 1,000 kilos = 2,204 pounds
• 1 container (20 ft) ≈ 20–25 tonnes
• 1 bag de açúcar geralmente pesa 50 kg

Use per para por unidade: 400 dollars per tonne, 8 dollars per bag.
Use of para ligar quantidade ao produto: ten tonnes of sugar, a bag of coffee.

💛 Dica: em inglês britânico se escreve tonne; em inglês americano, ton. Em Czarnikow, tonne.

grammarDeepDive.title: The verb to have — o segundo verbo essencial
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
O verbo to have (ter) muda na terceira pessoa:

• I / you / we / they → have
• he / she / it → has

• posse: I have a contract.
• experiência/responsabilidade: She has a meeting at 3.
• atividades rotineiras: We have lunch at 1.

💛 Dica: com coisas (the company, the team, the market), use sempre has: The company has offices worldwide.

grammarDeepDive.title: Time prepositions — on (dia), in (mês/ano), by (prazo)
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Três preposições de tempo essenciais:

• on + dia da semana ou data: on Friday, on the 15th, on March 2nd.
• in + mês, ano, estação, parte do dia: in March, in 2025, in summer, in the morning.
• by + prazo (não mais tardar que): by Friday, by the end of the month.

💛 Dica: by = até, no mais tardar. on = no dia exato. in = dentro do período.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entries.

grammarDeepDive.title: Days and frequency — always, usually, often, sometimes, never
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Dias da semana em inglês começam com letra maiúscula: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

Advérbios de frequência (do mais para o menos):
• always (sempre) 100%
• usually (geralmente) 80%
• often (frequentemente) 60%
• sometimes (às vezes) 40%
• never (nunca) 0%

Posição: antes do verbo principal mas depois do to be:
• I always check. (antes de check)
• I am always busy. (depois de am)

💛 Dica: on + dia (on Monday), at + fim de semana (at the weekend — UK) ou on the weekend (US).
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entries.

grammarDeepDive.title: Past Simple intro — write → wrote, send → sent
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
O Past Simple fala do que aconteceu no passado.

• Verbos regulares: adicione -ed: call → called, check → checked, sign → signed.
• Verbos irregulares: cada um tem sua forma. Os mais comuns em trade:
— write → wrote
— send → sent
— meet → met
— have → had
— go → went

💛 Dica: marcas de tempo no passado ajudam: yesterday, last week, this morning, two days ago.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entries.

grammarDeepDive.title: Can and could — pedir, oferecer, perguntar com educação
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Can e could são verbos modais — vêm antes de outro verbo (na forma base, sem to).

• can → habilidade, permissão, pedido informal: I can speak English. Can you help?
• could → pedido mais educado, possibilidade: Could you send the quote? We could meet tomorrow.
• Negativa: can't / cannot, couldn't / could not.

💛 Dica: em negócios, could soa mais profissional que can. Use Could you...? em e-mails e com clientes.

Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.

Adjetivos em inglês:

grammarDeepDive.title: Was and were — the past of to be
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
O passado do verbo to be:

• I / he / she / it → was
• you / we / they → were

Marcas de tempo comuns: yesterday, last week, last month, two days ago, in 2024.

Negativa: was not (wasn't), were not (weren't).
Pergunta: Was he at the office? Were they happy?

💛 Dica: uma frase por dia com yesterday I was... é ouro.
references: Murphy, R. — English Grammar in Use (Cambridge).
Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
Cambridge Dictionary — online entries.

grammarDeepDive.title: Review — putting it all together in one deal
grammarDeepDive.explanation:
Revisão das estruturas chave:

• to be: am/is/are (presente), was/were (passado).
• to have: have/has (presente), had (passado).
• Present Simple: rotinas → +s na terceira pessoa.
• Past Simple: regulares com -ed, irregulares (wrote, sent, met, was, had).
• Can / Could: pedido, habilidade, educação.
• There is / There are: existência.
• Preposições: on (dia), in (mês), by (prazo), per (por unidade), by + transporte.

💛 Dica final: releia suas 20 lições uma vez ao mês. Você vai se surpreender com seu progresso.

Eastwood, J. — Oxford Practice Grammar.
